# R370 v2 — segmented verifier route observation and corrected source provenance

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). This addendum supersedes v1's source-hash attribution and its blanket exclusion of verifier routes; v1 remains unchanged. Read-only source and URL audit. Only this report was created. No build, test, GPU/model run, profiler, service action, code change, or Git operation was performed. Main's active phase-cache work was not touched.

## Correction in one paragraph

V1 missed the `segmented_` branch in `Verifier::run`. On the current no-concurrent-host-USM configuration, `Verifier::run` runs one segment, calls `stream_sync(cs_)`, validates the completed ring, and only then calls the CPU pool with the host route IDs. The synchronization is already part of this execution path, so an aggregate at the callback entry needs no additional sync and can safely observe the route. This is the practical decode path under the task's `STRATA_VERIFY_SEGMENTED=1`, `STRATA_VERIFY_DEVICE_PLAN=0`, batch-off configuration. Only the **unsegmented** run/batch/pipelined paths that poll GPU-written host-USM signals without a completion boundary remain excluded. The route observer should be attached to the segmented `drive_pool_multi` callback used by this verifier path, not limited to `drive_pool`/`session_loop`.

## Source identity correction

The v1 table's SHA-256 values were read from the fixed-source worktree `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/diag-native-copy-queue-qualified-20261013`, commit `410904c99d273435b5302fa8976cc667d17957f2`; they were not hashes of the active, dirty `feat-phase-cache-stock-bench-20261013` worktree. The target worktree was dirty and changing under Main, so v1 did not capture a target-file SHA-256. This is a provenance correction, not a claim that the active worktree had those bytes.

For v2's verifier finding, I re-read both worktrees. In the fixed-source worktree at commit `410904c99d273435b5302fa8976cc667d17957f2`, `src/core/verify.cpp` SHA-256 is `efc5c8d37c1b6b18efa1a203c4ed8f0a4bc3c8c1098dbf0e87f8ab11cd845cad`; relevant lines are 1514-1618. In the active target worktree, HEAD was still `410904c99d273435b5302fa8976cc667d17957f2`, but the dirty `src/core/verify.cpp` SHA-256 was `1d4af800b20d07ae4d32ded551f76ddab450710cee4e5015c7a918289af5914d`; lines had shifted (launch around 1534, segment completion around 1567-1574, callback around 1594-1596, segment copy completion around 1599). The active version retains the same critical ordering. Since it was being edited concurrently, line-level design should be rechecked against Main's final tree before a patch. The fixed comparison worktree's original hashes for `generate.cpp`, `session.cpp`, `gpu.cpp` and `xe/router.cpp` remain as recorded in v1; they are fixed-tree hashes, not active-tree hashes.

## Safe decode seam in `Verifier::run`

In the fixed tree, `Verifier::run` starts at `src/core/verify.cpp:1441`; it selects the resident-only graph if `res_graph_ && all_resident()` (`1470`), otherwise captures the ordinary window. For the ordinary route:

1. The initial segment is launched at lines 1507-1515. `record_window` has already arranged for the GPU route producer and the host handoff to be part of the segment before it rings. The route producer itself is in `src/core/verify.cpp:982-1008`: topK writes `ids_`, and unless recording the special resident graph it calls `doorbell_publish` to copy the routed rows into `m_ids_` and ring `m_seq_` last.
2. In the service loop, `segmented_` calls `strata::gpu::stream_sync(cs_)` before reading the ring (`verify.cpp:1539-1554`, exact central lines 1547-1554 in fixed source). This is a normal queue completion wait. It is not a volatile/shared-memory poll. After successful return, the host checks `*seq` and calls the pool at lines 1574-1576 with `h_ids_ + tb*k`, `n`, `k`, and explicit layer `l`.
3. `drive_pool_split`/`drive_pool_multi` are in `src/program/generate.cpp:834-879`. In a one-stage target config, `drive_pool_multi` receives an explicit `layer`, sets `t->d.layers=layer`, then calls `expert_pool_dispatch_multi`. A route counter must copy/count `ids` at **callback entry**, before dispatch, using the explicit `layer`; do not infer layer by the mutable `Drive::d.layers` after dispatch.
4. The route handoff remains live through the callback and until the next segment reuses the mapping. Copy only the K IDs into the observer's fixed CPU-owned ring synchronously at callback entry. No pointer may be retained. After the callback, the existing `stream_sync(copy_)` at `verify.cpp:1577-1583` drains queued expert-copy operations before the next segment is launched (`1599-1607`). The route observer should not change the callback's existing copy or publication logic.

Under this segmented path, `stream_sync(cs_)` is per segment/layer (and per token group if `G=2`); it may already be a material execution cost, but telemetry adds no extra one. The metric is still observational: it tells which route IDs the existing path produced, not that the segment wait is free. Preserve the fixed source's existing behavior and benchmark it only through the stock comparison methodology if Main later authorizes that work.

`STRATA_VERIFY_SEGMENTED=1` forces segmented mode even if `host_handoff_concurrent(cs_)` reports true; otherwise source selects segmented mode when that capability is absent (`verify.cpp:415-421`). In the supplied hardware state the capability-based branch also selects it. `volatile`, `_mm_sfence`, and `atomic_thread_fence` elsewhere in Verifier do not provide this completion boundary; the safety finding relies specifically on the successful `stream_sync(cs_)` before callback entry.

## Condition matrix

| Verifier execution condition | Route observer decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `Verifier::run`, ordinary graph, `segmented_ == true`, pool callback present | **Include.** Aggregate at callback entry using explicit `layer`, `n`, `k`; route buffer is host-readable after the existing `stream_sync(cs_)`. | This is the serialized, queue-completed path at verify.cpp 1547-1576. No new synchronization is needed. |
| Same path, `device_plan_ == false` | **Include.** This is the supplied primary config. | Ordinary `doorbell_publish` copies routes; CPU computes misses as usual. |
| Same path, `device_plan_ == true`, ordinary (non-resident) graph | **Include route selection, label source/CPU-miss status separately.** | The `device_plan_` branch calls `resident_plan` at verify.cpp 1001-1005, but `doorbell_publish` still executes unless `recording_res_` (`1006-1008`). `Verifier::run` still calls `pool` after the segment sync. An all-resident group may leave no CPU expert jobs, but IDs are still real router output and safe to aggregate. Do not equate route count with CPU-served miss count. |
| `res == true` / `recording_res_` all-resident graph | **No callback; report this route segment as observer-ineligible/unobserved.** | `Verifier::run` chooses `exec_res_` at line 1514 and its per-layer service loop is conditioned on `!res` at line 1539. The special resident graph suppresses the host doorbell (`recording_res_` branch at 1006). Do not count it as zero routes or as a negative cache hit. |
| `Verifier::run`, `segmented_ == false` | **Exclude unless a different existing completion boundary is proved.** | It reads `h_seq_` in the spin loop before the later pool callback (verify.cpp 1555-1567 in fixed source); this is concurrent host-USM observation. V1 was right to reject this subcase, wrong to generalize it to all verifier paths. |
| Batch windows (`init_slots`, `run_slots`/`run_slot_rows`, `batch_poll`) when `segmented_ == true` | **Unavailable/rejected.** | `init_slots` explicitly errors at verify.cpp 1784-1788: batch requires qualified concurrent host-USM handoff. The batch route polling loop at 2053+ has no per-layer stream completion before callback; it relies on the concurrent handoff qualification. |
| Pipelined windows (`capture_all`, `prestage`, `pl_launch`, `service`) when `segmented_ == true` | **Unavailable/rejected.** | `capture_all` rejects `segmented_` at verify.cpp 2457-2463, and `prestage`/`pl_launch` reject unless `host_handoff_concurrent` (`2509+`, `2523+`). Thus the unsafe polling path is not reachable on this target configuration through those APIs. |
| `session_loop` single-token route | **Include** at `session.cpp:696-724` after `event_sync(probe)`, as described in v1. | Existing SYCL event completion boundary. |
| `session_run_token` token graph | **Exclude on current capability/configuration.** | It host-polls mapped sequence (`session.cpp:937-971`) and requires concurrent host handoff. |

The task says `batch=0/pipeline=1`; these names alone do not prove which API entered. For the route count to describe the served workload, the request should record an aggregate mode label from the actual path: `verify_run_segmented`, `session_loop`, `resident_graph_unobserved`, or `other_excluded`. Do not infer `Verifier::run` solely from a pipeline configuration flag. In particular, segmented `Verifier::run` is not the same as the explicitly pipelined-window API (`capture_all`/`pl_launch`/`service`).

## Updated implementation proposal

Keep the bounded observer contract from v1, but wire it into **both** safe callback families: `drive_pool` for `session_loop`, and `drive_pool_multi` for segmented `Verifier::run`. Restrict the multi callback to single-owner, non-batch ordinary run initially. At entry, before dispatch, validate and copy IDs from the callback's host handoff into a local fixed `std::array<int32_t,64>` (since the API admits K up to 64), then update the request observer using the explicit `layer` and `n_tok`. For the target model K=10. Do not allocate, log individual routes, or retain caller pointers. The observer state is owned by the serialized request driver, not `ExpertPool` workers; worker threads do not need route telemetry. If the actual application can call callbacks concurrently, use one fixed observer per issuer and merge after callback completion with CPU-only atomics or a lock; first confirm that concurrency from the caller. Never place counters in `ExpertDispatch` shared fields without proving ownership.

For a T-token verify window with `n_tok=T`, update W=2/4/8 sliding unions in per-layer reference counts over the observed route rows. A row is one token's K IDs for that layer; process all rows in deterministic token order and maintain W recent rows per layer. Collect min/median/p95/max and amortized unique packed bytes per completed window; count warm-up rows/windows separately. With the target MTP/spec path, rejected proposals are still actual verifier routes; label them by verifier-path position/window and do not claim accepted-output-only locality. If the question is decode emitted tokens only, retain separate attempted-route and committed-output denominators using the verifier's existing acceptance result, without storing IDs.

At the same callback, independently update static-profile top19 membership and cold-start LRU3/LRU19 simulations per layer, with request-scoped reset. Report entry hits and exact `blob_bytes(layer)`-weighted logical hit bytes separately. Static profile is `read_expert_profile`'s loaded ranked pairs (`generate.cpp:2316+`, cache setup around 3032+); preserve profile path/hash and per-layer available rank, and report unavailable if absent. LRU3 and LRU19 are independent policies. Do not let LRU's diagnostic state alter production residency or routing.

For segmented Verifier, if `device_plan_` means some routes are all GPU-resident and the CPU callback dispatch produces zero jobs, the observer still counts those IDs as **router selections**. Optionally count CPU misses/hits only from callback data/source classification already safely available, but keep these as separate signals. The observer should report `callbacks`, total routed rows, rows unobserved due to resident graph, route IDs invalid/duplicate, request reset ID/hash, and path counts. Aggregate only; no raw IDs, weights, prompt, per-layer traces, or repeated sync logs are retained.

The R369 v2 byte basis stays authoritative: 98,227,200 B for one expert across 48 layers; 982,272,000 B for ten per layer; W union values remain logical extent accounting. Do not infer actual physical transfers, HBM/DRAM traffic, throughput ceilings, or time saved from these values. For route reuse to warrant an implementation beyond diagnostic counters, require material byte-weighted LRU hit opportunity above static top19 on held-out decode requests, then a separately approved stock paired comparison with correctness and full decode distribution; this instrumentation alone cannot establish cache benefit.

## External source/link audit and limits

I opened the concrete URLs below and verified that the pages exist and contain the cited statements. These links provide context only; their numbers and hardware designs do not transfer to Strata.

* vLLM [`routed_experts_capturer.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts_capturer.py) exists. Its source describes worker-side routed expert capture into a device buffer and scheduler-side persistence; its docs explicitly distinguish capture support by router/kernel and record layout. This is a design example for route ownership and layout, not proof that Strata can safely poll host USM. The v1-specific claim about a NumPy fancy-index copy was **not reverified at the opened lines**, so v2 drops it.
* vLLM's [expert parallel deployment docs](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/docs/serving/expert_parallel_deployment.md) state that EPLB collects load statistics each forward and periodically redistributes expert mappings. This supports per-forward aggregation as an established systems pattern, but EPLB balances ranks and is not a temporal expert cache.
* SGLang's [expert parallelism docs](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/docs/advanced_features/expert_parallelism.mdx) describe its TopK-to-dispatch execution stages and EPLB using activation statistics to map/replicate experts. They do not substantiate local route-buffer ownership or cache policy gains.
* Intel [llm-scaler](https://github.com/intel/llm-scaler) is confirmed as a vLLM-based Intel serving project with XPU, quantization, and supported MoE models in its README. The inspected page does not establish a local temporal expert cache or its measurement methodology; v2 makes no such claim.
* The independent [moe-hotcache repository](https://github.com/ap03906101/moe-hotcache) exists and its README describes routing counters, pointer-table promotion, and quarantining an evicted slot for one cycle to protect in-flight graph users. These are repository-author claims (self-reported), not independently validated source review or a transferred performance claim. It supports the general lifetime concern for any future cache mutation, not this diagnostic's correctness.
* The [nothin personal blog post](https://nothiny.github.io/2026/09/15/mini-moe/) exists and contains the cited discussion of LRU/LFU/frequency-decay/LRU-K and its reported DeepSeek-V2-Lite cache results. This is a personal implementation report with its own workload and hardware; use it only to motivate measuring drift and independent LRU curves, not as an optimality or performance proof.
* vLLM [RFC #38256](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38256) exists. The opened discussion includes an implementation comment explaining that prompt-frequency estimates can become stale on topic shift and that Apple Silicon unified-memory results may not carry to discrete GPUs. It is a discussion/RFC, not merged product behavior.

Primary memory-order basis: the current [SYCL 2020 specification](https://registry.khronos.org/SYCL/specs/sycl-2020/html/sycl-2020.html?from=20423&from_column=20423) says host event waits block until represented actions complete, and its [host/device interaction reference](https://github.khronos.org/SYCL_Reference/iface/interaction-with-host-code.html) makes concurrent USM/atomic guarantees capability-dependent. Strata's `gpu::stream_sync` calls queue wait-and-throw in the fixed tree (`src/core/gpu.cpp`, stream synchronization implementation); `Verifier::run` calls it before route callback only in the segmented branch. This is the primary reason to admit segmented run observations and exclude unsegmented polling under supplied `ATOMIC_HOST_USM=0`; CPU fences alone do not replace device completion.

## Corrected decision

Proceed with the aggregate design for the route callback reached by `Verifier::run` when `segmented_` is true, plus the previously identified `session_loop` route after its `event_sync(probe)`. The task's current configuration should be measured through its actual segmented verifier route; blanket exclusion would miss the intended decode. Keep `device_plan_` as a route-selection observer inclusion, label route IDs separately from CPU-served misses, and treat `res_graph_` as unobserved because it skips the callback. Exclude unsegmented spin-polling, batch, and explicit pipelined-window APIs on this capability configuration. Existing event/queue completion only; no added sync or raw trace. Preserve v1 and consult this v2 for the corrected verifier finding.
